title: Chaffin 1990: centroid distance of rectus abdominis at L2-L3 (F, supine)

imaging.modality: CT (Technicare 1440 HPS), bone protocol 130 kV, 1-mm slices
imaging.plane: transverse scans perpendicular to the table at the disc levels (identified on scout view); x/y axes rotated so y passes through disc centroid and spinous process
imaging.posture_detail: supine, knees and hips flexed to minimise lordosis

quantity.name: centroid_distance
quantity.definition: distance from the vertebral-body (or disc) centroid to the muscle area centroid in the image plane; AP signed (+ anterior, - posterior), ML unsigned lateral distance. NOT a true moment arm

source.authors: Chaffin DB, Redfern MS, Erig M, Goldstein SA
source.sample: 96 women (scans: L2/L3 31, L3/L4 96, L4/L5 66); women aged 40-63 (osteoporosis-study CT population)

protocol.summary: Supine CT of 96 older women; area-weighted centroids from trapezoid tracing.
how_to_simulate: Pose the model supine with hips/knees flexed (reduced lordosis).
Cut a transverse plane (perpendicular to the body long axis) through the L2-L3 disc.
Take the area/PCSA-weighted centroid of rectus abdominis on each side; origin = disc centroid, y axis = disc centroid -> spinous process.
Report |x| (ML) and |y| (AP) and compare per side. Centroid distance, not a moment arm.

subject_model.source: Table 1 (whole sample) and Table 3 (disc area at this level)

protocol.notes: Authors call these moment arms (absolute x, y components). Segmental grand average column not stored. cm -> mm.

extraction.check_notes: All values verified cell by cell on rendered pages 12-13 (layout text had OCR errors).
